text:
Marathon Petroleum fell slightly today as crude oil prices dropped for a second consecutive day on hopes for a diplomatic resolution to the Iran conflict. Crude has retreated from recent highs, with U.S. oil now trading at $103.37 per barrel—down sharply from the geopolitical premium that had driven prices higher. For a refiner, lower oil prices can seem positive for margins in theory, but the market is evidently concerned that the immediate uncertainty driving energy higher has now reversed.

The stock's broader 10% decline over two weeks reflects investor caution ahead of the company's quarterly earnings announcement (which came today). A leadership change announced last week added to that uncertainty, and CNBC reporting flagged that Big Oil earnings guidance—not just reported profits—will be what investors scrutinize most closely going forward.
